note: PIAZZOLLA: the quintet tangos are entered with the scoring of Piazzolla's own Quinteto (bandoneon as accordion, violin, piano, electric guitar, double bass; first quintet 1960, second quintet 1978); years are given only where a source opened here states them. Left out (not entered, budget): Oblivion, Fugata, Soledad, Tres minutos con la realidad, Tanguedia and Camorra pieces beyond those entered, Chin Chin, Prepárense, La Camorra I-III, Tango Ballet (string orchestra) and the Sexteto and Octeto repertoire. Out of scope: Histoire du tango (flute and guitar), Le Grand Tango (cello and piano), Tango Suite (two guitars) and the violin-catalogue arrangements (ids 273 Desyatnikov, 1128-1130, 2183). EVIDENCE: Deezer album and track lists (the earlier lookups of this slice were cached; the albums cited by id were read in full or in grouped form), Apple composer searches and album lookups, MusicBrainz work lists and recording lookups, Wikipedia work lists (English, Spanish, Portuguese), the composers' own pages (Ortiz) and a few web searches. The IMSLP pages were not opened one by one: titles, years and publication dates of the IMSLP candidates come from the census input. Naxos Library, Presto and publisher pages (Boosey & Hawkes, Schott, Eschig, Peermusic) were not used, so no `published` field is filled except where the input names the first edition. OWNER MAY RULE: (1) Piazzolla's quintet tangos (bandoneon as accordion, with his own quintet scoring) are entered as chamber repertoire; the owner may prefer only the Kronos works and the Four Seasons. (2) The Four Seasons of Buenos Aires is one entry (form set) because the cycle is played as a group, although the four tangos were written separately (1965-70). (3) Villa-Lobos's Chôros No. 7 is a septet with tam-tam ad lib. (Wikipedia list), so the percussion is optional; IMSLP counts it as a part. (4) Toccata (sin fuga) is cross-listed with violin id 4789 although the only recording found is by the M-G-M Chamber Orchestra. (5) Medium or low confidence: Ginastera's Cantos del Tucumán and Impresiones de la Puna (MusicBrainz recordings, performers read from MusicBrainz), Golijov's Ever Yours and Tintype (a 2026 release by the Arethusa Quartet), Brouwer's String Quartet No. 4 and String Trio, Márquez's Homenaje a Gismonti, Ortiz's Aroma foliado and Lío de 4, Assad's Clash, López's La Caresse du Couteau (a live album on an own label), Nobre's Desafio XXXII, Chávez's Fuga H-A-G-C. (6) Years left blank where no opened source gives them (most Piazzolla tangos, Assad's Clash, López's quartet). (7) Golijov's Last Round is entered in its original scoring, two string quartets and double bass (nine players, IRCAM and Boosey as read in a web search); the Jupiter Quartet plays a string-quartet version whose arranger was not identified, so that version is not entered. NOT FOUND OR NOT CHECKED: no recording was found for Guarnieri's quartets and trios, Santoro, Orbón, Nobre's quartet, Lavista's Nos. 7-8, Ortiz's Corpórea and Pico-Bite-Beat, Golijov's Qohelet; Brouwer's piano trios, Assad's Four Scenes and Chávez's Sextet scoring were not settled. The Ortiz track 'Cuarteto No. 1' on a Quindecim disc could not be tied to her. Years of the Villa-Lobos quartets follow the IMSLP input (Wikipedia gives 1917 for No. 3 and 1948 for No. 11). Durations are rounded from the recordings cited, or taken from the composer's list (Ortiz).
